Modikwa Announces Major Investment to Expand South African Mining Operations

Modikwa, a leading player in South Africa’s metals and mining sector, has announced a significant expansion of its mining operations in the Limpopo province, underscoring renewed confidence in the region’s mineral potential. The investment, valued at R2.1 billion, aims to increase production capacity, modernize existing infrastructure, and create over 400 new jobs in the next three years.

“This expansion is a testament to our long-term commitment to South Africa and the local communities surrounding our operations,” said Sipho Dlamini, Modikwa’s Managing Director, at a press briefing on Thursday. “The additional capacity will allow us to better meet demand from both domestic and international markets, while also supporting economic development in Limpopo.”

According to industry analysts, the investment comes at a time of steady global demand for platinum group metals and chrome—two of the key resources extracted at Modikwa’s sites. “South Africa remains a vital source of PGMs, and Modikwa’s expansion is a positive signal for the sector,” commented Thandi Mokoena, a mining analyst at Malahle Advisory. “The project aligns with broader efforts to increase beneficiation and value addition within the country.”

The expansion includes upgrades to mining shafts, installation of advanced ore-handling systems, and enhanced worker safety facilities. Local suppliers are expected to benefit from procurement opportunities, with Modikwa committing to source at least 60% of new project spend from South African-owned businesses.

Community leaders have welcomed the announcement, citing the potential for job creation and skills development. “This investment brings hope for our youth and helps fight unemployment in the district,” said Refilwe Monareng, chairperson of the Sekhukhune Community Forum.

Modikwa’s expansion project is set to begin construction in September, with completion targeted for late 2026. The company confirmed that all environmental permits and regulatory approvals are in place. As the project moves forward, Modikwa has pledged ongoing engagement with stakeholders to ensure that local interests remain central to the development.
